title: Small organisms show a limited range of forms because molecular forces control them

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Small organisms show a limited range of forms because molecular forces control them

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because protozoa, bacteria and other minute cells are of a size at which form is mainly controlled by molecular forces, they exhibit only a limited range of forms, which vary with physical conditions.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. V: The Forms of Cells

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: To the fact that these little organisms belong to an order of magnitude in which form is mainly, if not wholly, conditioned and controlled by molecular forces, is due the limited range of forms which they actually exhibit.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter V, “The Forms of Cells”; topic “Limited range of forms in small organisms”. Scope: unicellular organisms, bacteria, spores and free cells

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch05-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.60

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Morphospace size and environmental plasticity are measurable with abundant images. The causal inference from limited forms to molecular control is confounded, and representative cross-scale sampling is not available.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify shape diversity across bacteria, protozoa, spores, and free cells and compare it with larger organisms after standardizing dimensionality and sampling; relate within-taxon changes to temperature, osmolarity, and material properties. The claim is supported if small-cell morphospace is consistently restricted and predictable from molecular-scale force models.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Sampling effort differs radically between micro- and macro-organisms.

Molecular-force dominance is not implied by low diversity alone.

A 'limited range' needs a defined metric and null model.

discriminating power: 0.4
data existence: 0.8

operationalizability: 0.6

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Bacterial shape compilations are large enough to show that described forms fall into a few classes, which addresses the descriptive half of the claim for prokaryotes. The causal half, control by molecular forces, is not a field in those databases, and the same limited menu is predicted by shared ancestry. Algal images broaden the taxa slightly without supplying the force measurements.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Count distinct form classes among bacteria, protozoa and other minute cells, and test whether that count is small and shifts with physical conditions in the way surface-tension surfaces would. A short list of forms that tracks temperature, medium or osmotic state would support the claim; a wide form range at the same small sizes, uncorrelated with physical conditions, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Protozoa are poorly represented next to bacteria.

Shape fields are coarse categories, so 'limited' depends on the coding scheme.

A short list of forms can be phylogenetic conservatism rather than molecular-force control.

fields.label: Dimension scores
